Column and fit-statistic tokens in table_regression()

Source: R/table_regression_tokens.R
table_regression_tokens.Rd

Two vector arguments – show_columns and show_fit_stats – accept named tokens that select what to display and in what order. All tokens are lowercase (snake_case for compound tokens). Group tokens ("all_b", "all_ame", ...) expand to a fixed vector of atomic tokens; see show_columns below.

show_columns – per-coefficient columns

Each token = one displayed column.

  • Coefficient family: "b", "beta" (standardized), "se", "ci", "t", "p".

  • Degrees of freedom: "df", those of each coefficient's t test, the df of tidy(). They can differ from row to row: the Satterthwaite df of a cluster-robust vcov = "CR2" or of an lmerTest fit, the containment df of an lme fit. A whole df prints without decimals, another with one (1.9). A z test leaves its cell blank, and so does a model of z tests beside one of t tests; the token is refused when no model of the table has a t test. The rows of a random effect or of a smooth term, which have no t, show a dash, as in the "t" column. The header reads df, ddl in French. Opt-in: no group token holds it.

  • Marginal effects: "ame", "ame_se", "ame_ci", "ame_p", "ame_df". "p" always refers to the B-coefficient p-value; for the AME-specific p-value use "ame_p". "ame_df" gives the degrees of freedom of each AME's t test (the Satterthwaite df under vcov = "CR2"), under the header of "df" and with its rules: blank under a z test, refused when no AME of the table has a t test.

  • Partial effect sizes – lm only: "partial_f2", "partial_eta2", "partial_omega2", each with a paired _ci companion ("partial_f2_ci", "partial_eta2_ci", "partial_omega2_ci").

  • Term-level test – lm, glm and mixed-effects models: "partial_chi2" and its twin "partial_f", the term-level test. By default (partial_type = "II") each term is tested under the marginality-respecting hypothesis that excludes any higher-order interaction containing it (the car::Anova(type = 2) convention), so the value does not depend on the factor coding. partial_type = "III" keeps the interactions and tests the term in a sum-to-zero coding (see partial_type in table_regression()). For glm the term-level test is the F that anova(reduced, full, test = "F") reports when the dispersion is estimated, the likelihood-ratio chi-square otherwise: "partial_f", \(F = (\Delta D / q) / \hat\phi\) on \((q, df)\) degrees of freedom, \(q\) the term's and \(df\) the residual degrees of freedom of the model, with \(\hat\phi\) the dispersion summary() estimates, for gaussian, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, Tweedie, MASS::negative.binomial(theta) fitted by glm() and the quasi families (the value car::Anova(type = 2, test.statistic = "F", error.estimate = "dispersion") reports; car's default Pearson estimate differs by the IRLS convergence error only, and drop1(test = "F") divides by the deviance dispersion instead); "partial_chi2", the likelihood-ratio chi-square (Long & Freese 2014 Sections 3.2.2, 3.2.4), for binomial, Poisson and MASS::glm.nb. For lm, "partial_f" is the F of car::Anova(type = 2) (type = 3 under partial_type = "III"), the F the variance-explained partials are built on, so a gaussian glm and its lm() twin print the same value. A token is refused when no model of the table carries it, and when a model carries the other one while that one is not requested (each test has its own column: ask for both). Both come from the refits and the model's own dispersion (the residual variance of an lm) whatever vcov. For the mixed models, "partial_chi2" is the Wald chi-square of the same hypothesis; see table_regression_mixed. Rendered as value (df) to disambiguate factor terms (k-1 df) from numeric terms (1 df), and the partial F as F (q, df) with both of its degrees of freedom, 3.45 (2, 28), as Stata and SAS report them: each cell carries the residual df of its own model, and the note defines the statistic only. The console and the rich outputs (tinytable, gt, flextable, Word, the clipboard) print the test in one column under the statistic's header, and Excel writes the statistic as a number with its df in the number format (0.00" (2, 28)"). output = "data.frame" and as_structured() keep the statistic and its df as numbers, in the statistic's column, then "<column>: df" and, for the F, "<column>: residual df". tidy() has them in df and df.residual, and inline() cites the statistic alone.

  • Variance explained per fit – lm only: "r2", "adj_r2". Like "n", these are per-fit columns: they are populated by table_regression_uv() screens, where each predictor block is its own model and the \(R^2\) answers "how much of the outcome does this predictor explain on its own". A model whose \(R^2\) is a single model-level number drops the column and reports it in the fit-statistics rows instead (the "r2" / "adj_r2" tokens of show_fit_stats, on by default for lm). Refused for classes with no least-squares variance partition (glm, coxph, ...), where only competing pseudo-\(R^2\) measures exist: name the one you want in show_fit_stats.

  • Sample columns: "n" – per-row N, populated by table_regression_uv() screens (each predictor block is its own fit); models without per-row N data drop the column. "n_events" – outcome event counts as events/N, per factor level (reference row included) and model totals on continuous rows, computed on each model's own estimation sample (STROBE item 16's "data behind the measures of association"; NEJM-style no. of events/total no.). Binary (binomial) outcomes and right-censored coxph fits – other models raise spicy_invalid_input.

  • Survival estimands – coxph and survreg: "rmst", "rmst_se", "rmst_ci", "rmst_p" (restricted-mean- survival-time difference over [0, tau]) and "risk_diff", "risk_diff_se", "risk_diff_ci", "risk_diff_p" (cumulative-incidence difference at at_time), by g-computation from the fitted model with bootstrap inference. The horizon arguments are required; see tau / at_time in table_regression() and table_regression_survival.

  • Bayesian fits: "pd" (probability of direction) and "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "mcse" (per-coefficient sampler diagnostics and the Monte Carlo standard error of the displayed posterior median), all-Bayesian tables only; see table_regression_bayesian.

Group tokens (presets) expand to a fixed atomic vector before validation:

  • "all_b" -> c("b", "se", "ci", "p")

  • "all_b_compact" -> c("b", "se", "p")

  • "all_b_full" -> c("b", "se", "ci", "t", "p")

  • "all_beta" -> c("b", "beta", "se", "ci", "p")

  • "all_ame" -> c("ame", "ame_se", "ame_ci", "ame_p")

  • "all_ame_compact" -> c("ame", "ame_p")

  • "all_f2" / "all_eta2" / "all_omega2" -> partial_* + its _ci companion.

Mix groups and atomic tokens: show_columns = c("all_b", "ame", "ame_p"). Duplicates after expansion are deduplicated; the order of tokens controls the order of the displayed columns. If standardized != "none" and "beta" is not already requested, it is auto-injected after "b". Asking for "beta" while standardized = "none" raises spicy_invalid_input.

Default (show_columns = NULL) is context-aware: "all_b" for a single model (the layout of the APA Manual 7 sample regression tables, Tables 7.16 and 7.17, pp. 219-220), "all_b_compact" for two or more models (CI dropped to fit the side-by-side layout; restore it explicitly when needed).

Fit statistics alone (show_columns = "none"): no coefficient row or column. Each model has one column, headed by its label (the outcome, "Model 1", a name of the list or model_labels, as for the column groups of the full table; "Model 1" for a single model), and the rows are the fit statistics of show_fit_stats, in its order, the change rows of nested = TRUE included. The title is the one of the full table; the note keeps what describes the models and their fit, and leaves out what describes coefficients. Models with different outcomes get an Outcome row when the column headers do not name them (outcome_labels = FALSE removes it). "none" goes alone, and show_fit_stats = FALSE is refused with it, as is layout = "stacked"; an empty show_columns (character(0), FALSE) is an error that points to "none". The arguments that act on coefficients only are ignored, with one spicy_ignored_arg warning naming those set to other than their default: ci_level, ci_method, tau, at_time, standardized, exponentiate, ame_type, p_adjust, keep, drop, show_intercept, show_thresholds, show_components, intercept_position, factor_layout, reference_style, reference_label, fit_stats_layout, show_re, re_scale, re_columns, re_test, re_ci, stars, effect_size_digits, and vcov, cluster and boot_n unless nested = TRUE (where a robust vcov gives the Wald change rows). An information criterion (AIC, BIC, deviance, ...) shown for models fitted to different numbers of observations or to different outcomes raises a spicy_caveat warning: its differences compare nothing. tidy() returns no row, glance() one row per model, and inline() cites a statistic of a model: inline(tbl, "aic", model = 2). table_regression_uv() refuses the token.

show_fit_stats – model-level rows below the coefficients

  • Counts: "nobs", "weighted_nobs", "n_events" (Cox models: number of events, reported alongside n per the field convention; blank for other classes). "nobs" and the BIC follow the engine's stats::nobs(), which for a weighted polr or clm fit is the sum of the weights.

  • Variance explained: "r2" and "adj_r2" (least-squares fits: linear, robust, instrumental-variable and feols; "r2" alone for rms::ols, "adj_r2" alone for GAMs), "omega2" (lm only).

  • \(R^2\) outside least squares (glm, polr, clm, multinom and rms::lrm fits): "pseudo_r2_tjur" (Tjur 2009; binomial models only), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (McFadden 1974), "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke" (Nagelkerke 1991) and "r2_deviance" (Cameron & Windmeijer 1997; glm families other than the binomial). What each one computes, and which a family shows by default, is in R-squared of glm and categorical models in table_regression().

  • Pseudo-\(R^2\) of a beta regression (betareg::betareg only, on request): "pseudo_r2_ferrari", the squared correlation between the linear predictor of the mean and the response on the scale of the mean link (Ferrari & Cribari-Neto 2004), the value summary() reports.

  • Residual scale: "sigma", "rmse". "sigma" is the lm \(\hat{\sigma}\). For glm and the GLM-like fixest fits, it is the square root of the dispersion (so a gaussian glm reads as lm), and 1 when the family fixes it (binomial, Poisson). For survreg, it is the scale \(\sigma\) of \(\log T = X'\beta + \sigma W\) for the distributions fitted on \(\log T\) (the standard deviation of \(\log T\) for the log-normal), and of \(T = X'\beta + \sigma W\) for those that model \(T\) itself (gaussian, logistic, extreme value, t), blank when strata give one scale per stratum. For glmmTMB, it is the same square root for the gaussian, Gamma and Tweedie families, and the fixed 1 of Poisson and binomial. It is blank for the negative-binomial and beta fits below, whose dispersion has its own row, and for the other glmmTMB families, whose sigma() is a family-specific parameter. For mgcv::gam and bam, a glm family follows the glm rule; an extended family shows the square root of its scale only when the GAM estimates one (tw()), and is blank otherwise (an estimated nb(), betar(), scat(), ziP(), ocat()): mgcv fixes their scale at 1.

  • Survey designs (survey::svyglm only): "eff_p", the effective number of parameters of the design (the first element of survey's extractAIC, the sum of the Rao-Scott eigenvalues). Opt-in and distinct from "aic", which reports the design-based AIC of Lumley & Scott (2015). Blank for other classes.

  • Bayesian fits only: "r2_bayes" (posterior-median Bayesian \(R^2\), Gelman et al. 2019 – in the all-Bayesian default), "elpd_loo" and "looic" (PSIS-LOO expected log predictive density and its deviance-scale twin, Vehtari et al. 2017; opt-in, a few seconds per model; the footer discloses the elpd standard error), and "waic" (Watanabe-Akaike; PSIS-LOO is generally preferred). See table_regression_bayesian.

  • Negative-binomial dispersion. NB2 fits (MASS::glm.nb, lme4::glmer.nb, fixest::fenegbin, mgcv::gam with nb(), pscl::zeroinfl and pscl::hurdle with dist = "negbin", whose theta is that of the count part, and glmmTMB with nbinom2 or truncated_nbinom2): "theta" (\(V = \mu + \mu^2/\theta\)) and "alpha" (\(= 1/\theta\), the Stata nbreg convention). NB1 fits (glmmTMB with nbinom1 or truncated_nbinom1): "delta" (\(V = \mu(1 + \delta)\), the \(\delta\) of Stata's nbreg, dispersion(constant)).

  • Beta precision: "phi". In beta regression (betareg::betareg, mgcv::gam with betar(), and glmmTMB with beta_family()), \(Var(y) = \mu(1-\mu)/(1+\phi)\) (Ferrari & Cribari-Neto 2004; higher \(\phi\) = less dispersion). For glmmTMB with betabinomial() or ordbeta(), \(\phi\) is the precision parameter of the beta part. A constant precision is back-transformed from its link, so y ~ x | 1 reports the same \(\phi\) as y ~ x.

  • For these dispersion rows ("theta", "alpha", "delta", "phi"), a column whose model lacks the parameter is blank, so a Poisson model can stand beside an NB2 model, or NB1 beside NB2. A parameter fixed in the call is not an estimate and has no row: MASS::negative.binomial(theta) in glm(), mgcv's negbin(theta), and nb(theta) or betar(theta) with theta > 0. Such a negative-binomial model keeps the glm rule for "sigma". A negative-binomial glmer() always shows its theta, which lme4 counts in the degrees of freedom of the model: a glmer.nb() fit, its update() refits, and a glmer() with negative.binomial(theta). For mgcv::gam and bam, theta and phi are estimated with the smoothing parameters (REML by default), so they differ from the maximum-likelihood values of glm.nb(), betareg or glmmTMB. method = "ML" gives those. A token is refused only when no model in the table has the parameter, or when a model of that family has dispersion covariates (a glmmTMB dispformula, or a betareg y ~ x | z), so the parameter is not a single number. Those covariates are shown as a block of rows instead (show_components): Precision for a betareg y ~ x | z and a beta_family() dispformula, Dispersion for the other glmmTMB families.

  • GEE (geepack::geeglm only): "qic" and "qicu" – the quasi-likelihood information criteria (Pan 2001; QIC for working-correlation choice, QICu for covariate choice) via geepack::QIC(), computed only when requested (QIC silently refits the independence working model); "scale" – the estimated scale (dispersion) parameter, shown only when the fit estimated it (blank under scale.fix = TRUE, matching geepack's own summary); "max_cluster_size" – the largest cluster in the estimation sample (on by default with "n_groups", which renders the N (<id>) cluster count). Cluster statistics count the clusters geepack itself used (geese$clusz, consecutive runs of id = values), so they always describe the displayed sandwich inference. Refused when no model in the table is a geeglm fit; the likelihood-based tokens ("aic", pseudo-\(R^2\), ...) are refused in return for all-GEE tables – quasi-likelihood has no likelihood.

  • Absorbed fixed effects (fixest fits, and estimatr fits built with fixed_effects =): "fixed_effects" renders a Fixed effects: block at the top of the fit statistics – one Yes / No row per absorbed factor (the etable / esttab convention), blank cells for models without the concept in mixed tables – and is on by default for both. Varying-slope-only factors (Origin[[x]]) absorb no intercept: they read No when another model absorbs that factor, and contribute no row otherwise. "within_r2" is the FE-partialed within R-squared (a default for feols, except an IV one; opt-in for estimatr; GLM-family fixest fits report fixest's McFadden pr2 instead). Both tokens are refused when no model in the table absorbs fixed effects.

  • Effect size: "f2".

  • Information criteria: "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance" (lowercase like every other token; the rendered row labels stay AIC / AICc / BIC). The AIC and BIC of a fixest model are those of its lm(), glm() or MASS::glm.nb() twin with the fixed effects as dummies: glm()'s log-likelihood for a Gaussian, Gamma or inverse-Gaussian feglm(), with the residual variance, dispersion or theta counted, which fixest's AIC() leaves out. A Gaussian femlm() follows the same rule; Poisson, binomial and IV fits keep fixest's values. A lean fit (lean = TRUE) that lost what they need, its weights or the fitted values of a Gamma or inverse-Gaussian feglm(), shows no AIC, BIC or nested rows. A survey-design fit has no likelihood: "deviance", "bic", "aicc", the pseudo-R-squared tokens and "r2_deviance" are refused for a table of design fits, and "aic" when no model of the table is a svyglm.

  • Log-likelihood: "log_lik", the value of stats::logLik(), from which the AIC row is computed. It is the restricted log-likelihood of a model fitted by REML, and for a binomial glm() it is logLik()'s value whatever the layout of the data: it includes the binomial coefficients of a grouped response and rounds non-integer weights, unlike the pseudo-\(R^2\) rows. A column whose model has no likelihood (a quasi family, a survey design, GEE, two-stage least squares) shows a dash; the token is refused when no model of the table has one, and for Bayesian fits.

  • Cox models (survival::coxph and survey::svycoxph): "concordance", Harrell's C, the value summary() reports. When the row is shown, the concordance leaves the note, which otherwise gives it with its standard error. rms::cph fits have no concordance row or note.

  • Change-stats for hierarchical comparison (active under nested = TRUE; see Hierarchical (nested) model comparison in table_regression()): "r2_change", "adj_r2_change", "f_change", "f2_change", "lrt_change", "aic_change", "aicc_change", "bic_change", "deviance_change", "p_change". The differences, current model minus previous ("r2_change", "adj_r2_change", "f2_change", and the AIC, AICc and BIC changes), print with an explicit sign (+0.07, -9.4) in every output. The test statistics and "p_change" are never signed. The test statistics carry their degrees of freedom, as the partial F cell does: 12.38 (1, 29) for an F, the number of added parameters and the residual df of the larger model (the denominator df for the Wald F of a robust vcov), 9.12 (1) for a chi-square. A df that is not a whole number (the HTZ denominator under "CR2", the df of a smooth term) prints with one decimal, 174.77 (2, 0.8). The rich outputs print the same cell, inline() cites the statistic alone, output = "data.frame" keeps it as a number, and Excel writes the number with the df in its number format. "deviance_change" is the drop in deviance (previous minus current), positive when the larger model fits better, and is not signed either.

Default (resolved when NULL) is class-aware: lm and lm_robust fits get c("nobs", "r2", "adj_r2"); glm, mgcv::gam, polr, clm, multinom, rms::lrm and rms::Glm fits get "nobs", the \(R^2\) rows of their family (see R-squared of glm and categorical models) and "aic"; mixed lm + glm sets union both groups (the renderer per-row en-dashes the inappropriate cell); coxph and cph fits get c("nobs", "n_events", "aic"), and a svycoxph fit gets c("nobs", "weighted_nobs", "n_events"), since a design-based fit has no AIC; GEE fits get c("nobs", "n_groups", "max_cluster_size") (the cluster structure, Stata xtgee-header style). When nested = TRUE, the class-aware default is extended with change tokens (c("r2_change", "f_change", "p_change") for lm, c("lrt_change", "p_change") for glm, c("f_change", "p_change") for a glm whose dispersion is estimated). The order of tokens in show_fit_stats controls the order of the rows.

Fit statistics by model class

For each class of table_regression_models(), the rows a one-model table shows under the default show_fit_stats (Default), in their order, then every token that gives a row when named (Available). A parenthesis after a token gives the fits it is limited to. The change tokens need nested = TRUE and are not listed. The same lists are the columns fit_stats_default and fit_stats of table_regression_models().

Linear and generalized linear

  • lm. Default: "nobs", "r2", "adj_r2". Available: "nobs", "weighted_nobs" (weighted fit), "r2", "adj_r2", "omega2", "sigma", "rmse", "f2", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

  • glm. Default: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial logit, binary outcome), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson), "r2_deviance" (Gaussian, Gamma), "aic" (not quasi). Available: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson), "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke" (binomial, Poisson), "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial), "r2_deviance" (not binomial), "sigma", "rmse", "aic" (not quasi), "aicc" (not quasi), "bic" (not quasi), "deviance", "log_lik" (not quasi).

  • negbin. Default: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "aic". Available: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke", "r2_deviance", "theta", "alpha", "rmse", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

  • rlm. Default: "nobs". Available: "nobs", "sigma", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • nls. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "sigma", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

Robust, IV, quantile, panel

  • lm_robust. Default: "fixed_effects" (with fixed_effects =), "nobs", "r2", "adj_r2". Available: "nobs", "r2", "adj_r2", "fixed_effects" (with fixed_effects =), "within_r2" (with fixed_effects =), "n_groups" (with fixed_effects =).

  • iv_robust. Default: "nobs". Available: "nobs", "r2", "adj_r2".

  • ivreg. Default: "nobs". Available: "nobs", "r2", "adj_r2".

  • tobit. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "sigma", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • rq. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "aic", "aicc", "log_lik".

  • fixest. Default: "fixed_effects" (with fixed effects), "nobs", "r2" (feols, not IV), "within_r2" (feols with fixed effects, not IV), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (GLM family), "aic" (not IV). Available: "nobs", "r2" (feols), "adj_r2" (feols), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (GLM family), "theta" (negative binomial), "alpha" (negative binomial), "fixed_effects" (with fixed effects), "within_r2" (feols with fixed effects), "n_groups" (with fixed effects), "sigma" (not negative binomial), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

Mixed effects

Available: "nobs", "theta" (NB2 family, no dispersion formula), "alpha" (NB2 family, no dispersion formula), "delta" (NB1 family, no dispersion formula), "phi" (beta family, no dispersion formula), "r2_marginal" (no ordinal or beta family, zero-inflation or dispersion formula), "r2_conditional" (no ordinal, beta or truncated family, zero-inflation or dispersion formula), "n_groups", "icc" (Gaussian, no dispersion formula), "sigma" (Gaussian, Gamma, Poisson, binomial or Tweedie family, no dispersion formula), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance" (no ordinal, truncated or beta family), "log_lik".

  • lme. Default: "nobs", "n_groups", "icc", "r2_marginal", "r2_conditional", "aic", "bic". Available: "nobs", "r2_marginal", "r2_conditional", "n_groups", "icc", "sigma", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • mlogit. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • hurdle. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "theta" (negative binomial), "alpha" (negative binomial), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

Survival

  • coxph. Default: "nobs", "n_events", "aic". Available: "nobs", "n_events", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik", "concordance".

  • survreg. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "sigma" (no strata), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • cph. Default: "nobs", "n_events", "aic". Available: "nobs", "n_events", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • flexsurvreg. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

Survey-weighted

  • svyglm. Default: "nobs", "weighted_nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "weighted_nobs", "aic", "eff_p".

  • svyolr. Default: "nobs", "weighted_nobs". Available: "nobs", "weighted_nobs".

  • svycoxph. Default: "nobs", "weighted_nobs", "n_events". Available: "nobs", "weighted_nobs", "n_events", "concordance".

Population-averaged (GEE)

  • geeglm. Default: "nobs", "n_groups", "max_cluster_size". Available: "nobs", "qic", "qicu", "scale", "max_cluster_size", "n_groups".

Additive, proportions, selection

  • gam. Default: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial logit, binary outcome), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial), "r2_deviance" (Gaussian, Gamma, Tweedie), "aic" (not quasi). Available: "nobs", "adj_r2", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial), "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke" (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial), "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial), "r2_deviance" (nb, tw or a glm family but binomial), "theta" (nb()), "alpha" (nb()), "phi" (betar()), "sigma" (glm family or tw()), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

  • betareg. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_ferrari", "phi", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

  • selection. Default: "nobs", "aic". Available: "nobs", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "log_lik".

rms

  • ols. Default: "nobs", "r2". Available: "nobs", "r2", "sigma", "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

  • lrm. Default: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binary outcome), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "aic". Available: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden", "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke", "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binary outcome), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

  • Glm. Default: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial logit, binary outcome), "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson), "r2_deviance" (Gaussian, Gamma), "aic". Available: "nobs", "pseudo_r2_mcfadden" (binomial, Poisson), "pseudo_r2_nagelkerke" (binomial, Poisson), "pseudo_r2_tjur" (binomial), "r2_deviance" (not binomial), "aic", "aicc", "bic", "deviance", "log_lik".

Bayesian

  • stanreg. Default: "nobs", "r2_bayes". Available: "nobs", "r2_bayes", "elpd_loo", "looic", "waic".

  • brmsfit. Default: "nobs", "r2_bayes". Available: "nobs", "r2_bayes", "elpd_loo", "looic", "waic".

table_regression() for the arguments; table_regression_models() for the registry of supported classes; the pages of the model families listed under Pages by model family in table_regression().

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
print(table_regression(
  fit,
  show_columns = c("all_b", "ame"),
  show_fit_stats = c("nobs", "r2", "sigma", "aic")
))
